desired_performances: Given a monitoring dashboard, interpret degradation signals, differentiate likely causes, and propose a response action.

objectives.performance: Interpret degradation signals on a monitoring dashboard
conditions: Given a monitoring dashboard with model performance metrics
success_criteria: Correctly identifies which metrics indicate degradation
Explains what each degradation signal means for model behavior

assumption_notes: Assumes learner needs to understand metric interpretation before cause differentiation

objectives.performance: Differentiate likely causes of model degradation
conditions: Given interpreted degradation signals from monitoring data
success_criteria: Distinguishes between data drift, concept drift, and operational issues
Provides reasoning for why certain causes are more likely than others

assumption_notes: Assumes learner can build on signal interpretation to infer causation

objectives.performance: Propose appropriate response actions to model degradation
conditions: Given identified degradation causes and organizational constraints
success_criteria: Proposes action that addresses the identified cause
Justifies the response with reference to signals and diagnosis

assumption_notes: Assumes learner can synthesize interpretation and diagnosis into actionable recommendations

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can interpret monitoring signals, differentiate causes, and propose response actions

required_evidence.criterion: Correctly identifies at least two degradation signals from dashboard data
Provides a plausible cause diagnosis with supporting reasoning
Proposes a response action consistent with the diagnosed cause

task.description: Given a monitoring dashboard showing model performance over time, identify degradation signals, diagnose the most likely cause, and propose a response action with justification.
conditions: Dashboard includes accuracy, latency, input distribution statistics, and error rate over 30-day period
No access to production systems, response is recommendation only

performance_levels: Does not identify relevant degradation signals
Identifies at least one signal but misinterprets meaning
Correctly identifies and interprets multiple signals
Does not propose a cause or proposes implausible cause
Proposes plausible cause with weak or missing reasoning
Proposes plausible cause with clear supporting reasoning
Proposes action unrelated to diagnosed cause
Proposes action aligned with cause but lacks justification
Proposes action aligned with cause and provides clear justification

scoring.mastery_rule: Learner achieves highest level on at least two dimensions and middle level on the third

assumption_notes: Assessment assumes dashboard scenario can be represented without live system access
Scoring assumes three-level rubric is sufficient for research purposes

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can identify and interpret degradation signals

required_evidence.criterion: Identifies at least one signal of model degradation from provided metrics

task.description: Review three monitoring charts and identify which ones show model degradation, explaining what each signal indicates.
conditions: Charts provided as static images or data tables

assumption_notes: Formative check supports objective 1 before progressing to cause differentiation

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can differentiate causes of degradation

required_evidence.criterion: Correctly distinguishes between at least two types of degradation causes

task.description: Given descriptions of three degradation scenarios, classify each as data drift, concept drift, or operational issue, with brief justification.
conditions: Scenarios presented as text descriptions with accompanying metric summaries

assumption_notes: Formative check prepares learner for integrated summative assessment

prerequisites.capability: Read and interpret line charts and time-series data
prerequisites.rationale: Monitoring dashboards typically display metrics as time series; learner must interpret trends and anomalies

prerequisites.capability: Understand basic ML model performance metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, latency)
prerequisites.rationale: Learner must know what metrics mean before interpreting degradation signals

prerequisites.capability: Understand concepts of data drift, concept drift, and model deployment
prerequisites.rationale: Differentiating causes requires familiarity with common degradation mechanisms

prerequisites.capability: Understand typical ML operations response strategies (retraining, rollback, feature engineering)
prerequisites.rationale: Proposing actions requires knowledge of available intervention options

prerequisites.capability: Familiarity with production ML system architecture
prerequisites.rationale: Understanding system context helps learner make realistic recommendations but is not strictly required for the core capability

sequencing_rationale: Module 1 establishes interpretation skills before moving to causal reasoning
Module 2 builds on signal interpretation to teach cause differentiation
Module 3 synthesizes prior modules to teach action planning
Module 4 provides integrated practice matching the summative assessment format

assumption_notes: Sequencing assumes linear dependency from interpretation to diagnosis to action
Time estimates assume learner has prerequisites and focus on new skill acquisition

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner recognizes common degradation signals in monitoring metrics
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner reviews annotated dashboard examples showing accuracy drop, latency increase, and input distribution shift

assumption_notes: Assumes annotated examples can convey signal patterns without live interaction

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner practices identifying degradation signals from unlabeled monitoring data
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner analyzes three monitoring charts and identifies which metrics show degradation, then receives feedback

assumption_notes: Practice reinforces pattern recognition from lesson 1

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner understands distinctions between data drift, concept drift, and operational causes
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner follows along as instructor works through a case showing data drift diagnosis, highlighting reasoning steps

assumption_notes: Worked example models diagnostic reasoning process

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner practices differentiating causes across multiple scenarios
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner classifies three degradation scenarios by cause type and explains reasoning, then receives feedback

assumption_notes: Practice reinforces differentiation criteria from lesson 3

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner understands how to match response actions to diagnosed causes
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner observes instructor propose and justify a response action for a given degradation scenario

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner practices proposing response actions with justification
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner receives a degradation scenario, proposes a response action, and writes a brief justification

assumption_notes: Independent practice prepares learner for summative assessment

lessons.lesson_goal: Learner integrates signal interpretation, cause diagnosis, and action planning in a single scenario
lessons.expected_learner_activity: Learner completes summative assessment: interprets dashboard, diagnoses cause, and proposes response with justification

assumption_notes: Integrated practice matches summative assessment task structure

special_review_question: Ignoring machine traceability or schema issues, is this instructional design pedagogically reasonable?
